name: St. Patrick's Day
h1: St. Patrick's Day Charcuterie Board Ideas
seo_title: St. Patrick's Day Charcuterie Board Ideas (Irish + Green)
description: St. Patrick's Day charcuterie board ideas: an Irish pub board with cheddar and stout, a shamrock board, an all-green board, a rainbow board for kids, and how much to buy.
answer: Build a St. Patrick's Day board around Irish flavors and the color green: an aged Irish cheddar, cooked ham or corned beef, brown soda bread and oatcakes, grainy mustard, and green apples, grapes and pickles. Shape it like a shamrock, pour a stout or a dry cider, and plan about 2 oz each of cheese and meat per guest before a meal.

ideas.title: The Irish Pub Board
ideas.text: Aged Irish cheddar, cooked ham and corned beef, whole-grain mustard, soda bread and oatcakes, pickled onions and green apple. Serve it with a stout or a dry cider.

ideas.title: The All-Green Board
ideas.text: Everything green: green grapes, kiwi, cucumber, Castelvetrano olives, pistachios, pesto and an herbed goat cheese, with plain crackers to carry it all.

ideas.title: The Rainbow Board
ideas.text: An arc of fruit and mild cheese in rainbow order (strawberries, mandarins, pineapple, green grapes, blueberries) ending in a 'pot of gold' bowl of cheese crackers.

shapes.name: Shamrock Board
steps: On a round board, set three small round bowls or cheese wheels close together as the leaves.
Surround each leaf with green: grapes, cucumber, olives and herbs.
Add a stem of pretzel rods or a line of crackers, and fill the gaps with cheddar and ham.

shapes.name: Rainbow Board
steps: On a rectangle, lay arcs of fruit in rainbow order, from strawberries on the outside to blueberries on the inside.
Set a cloud of white cheese cubes at one end.
Put a bowl of cheese crackers or gold-wrapped chocolate coins at the other end as the pot of gold.

plan.what: Buy crackers, oatcakes, mustard, pickles and the stout or cider.
Slice the ham and cheese, wash the fruit and fill the bowls. Cover and chill.
Take the cheddar out of the fridge and build the board.

faq.q: What goes on a St. Patrick's Day charcuterie board?
faq.a: An aged Irish cheddar, cooked ham or corned beef, soda bread or oatcakes, whole-grain mustard, pickles, and plenty of green: grapes, green apple, cucumber, olives and pistachios.

faq.q: What Irish cheese is good on a board?
faq.a: Aged Irish cheddar is the easy choice and most large grocery stores carry it. A cheese counter may also have Irish farmhouse cheeses, including washed-rind, blue and goat's milk styles. If you can't find Irish cheese, an aged white cheddar works.

faq.q: What drink goes with an Irish charcuterie board?
faq.a: A stout's roasted bitterness is a good match for sharp cheddar and salty ham. A dry cider is lighter and pairs with the apple and pickles. For a non-alcoholic option, try sparkling apple cider.

faq.q: How do you make a shamrock-shaped charcuterie board?
faq.a: Set three round bowls or small cheese wheels close together as the leaves, surround each with green food, and add a stem of pretzel rods or crackers. Fill the gaps with cheddar, ham and crackers.

faq.q: How much should I buy for a St. Patrick's Day party?
faq.a: As an appetizer before a meal, plan about 2 oz of cheese and 2 oz of meat per guest, plus 6 to 8 crackers. If the board is the party food, plan 3 oz of each and 10 to 12 crackers; if it's dinner, 4 oz of each. From 20 guests, add 10%.
